Messages.Author: Sao lee
Messages.Body:
Hi all,
I'm not quite clear about this contested card stuff... It usually
doesn't come up in my games, but it did yesterday, so I'm hoping to
clear it up for the future.

if a vampire is contested, does it become uncontrolled? Can you
withdraw blood from it? If not, can you still perform actions with it?

What if it has some nasty equipment on it, like talbot's chainsaw?

Also, if anyone could tell me a url where i could get some ancient
hearts and sabbat cards cheap, i'd be very happy :)

Sao lee

Messages.Author: TheLa...@hotmail.com
Messages.Body:
In article <3633b1a...@news.rotterdam.luna.net>,
S.P.War...@student.hro.nl (Sao lee) wrote:
> Hi all,

> if a vampire is contested, does it become uncontrolled?

It does _not_ move to your uncontrolled region. Effectively,
The vampire leaves play until it becomes uncontested.

>Can you withdraw blood from it?

No.

>If not, can you still perform actions with it?

No.

> What if it has some nasty equipment on it, like talbot's chainsaw?

You cannot access any equipment, cannot transfer its equipment,
cannot take actions, cannot react, cannot use abilities based
upon master cards played on that vampire. When a vampire is
contested you cannot use it in any way.

> hearts and sabbat cards cheap, i'd be very happy :)

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Sao lee wrote:
> I'm not quite clear about this contested card stuff... It usually
> doesn't come up in my games, but it did yesterday, so I'm hoping to
> clear it up for the future.
>

> if a vampire is contested, does it become uncontrolled?

Not exactly, but close. It becomes "out of play" for all
purposes (except for contesting).

> Can you
> withdraw blood from it?

No - it isn't really returned to the uncontrolled region.

> If not, can you still perform actions with it?

No - it is out of play in that regard as well.

> What if it has some nasty equipment on it, like talbot's chainsaw?

The minion cards (equipment, retainers, etc.) on it are also out of
play (except for the possibility of being contested themselves, should
a second copy come out).

> Also, if anyone could tell me a url where i could get some ancient
> hearts and sabbat cards cheap, i'd be very happy :)

I'll leave this one for someone in a non-official capacity.

: Not exactly, but close. It becomes "out of play" for all

This reminds me - what happens when a vamp stolen with Malk Dementia
becomes contested? (This came up in a game I was in last week - although
the vamp didn't actually get contested since I didn't want to contest
it. Though maybe I should have.)

The situation would be that the vamp is stolen during the Dementing player's
master phase, and then becomes contested sometime before that player's
next turn. Does the Dementing player then choose whether to pay the
contesting cost? Or is the Dementia return-control-to-rightful-owner
effect able to find the Demented Malk even though the vamp is currently
out of play?

(I would think that the Dementia can't find the Malk until it is no longer
contested, but then I'm not sure if it would still want to return control
at that point since the Dementing player's 'next untap phase' has come
and gone.)

Josh

Silly rabbit, Trix are for kids. ^_^ I have some experience with how
self-contesting works... what I was talking about is what happens when
a Malkavian under the influence of Malkavian Dementia becomes contested.
eg, John plays Malk Dementia to steal Bryan's Normal (his grandpredator,
my prey). I (John's prey) bring out my own Normal, making Normal contested.
Bryan takes his turn. Jon (other Jon) takes his turn. It comes around to
Dementing John's turn: He returns that Normal to Bryan without paying for
the contest. On my turn I will have to pay to contest Normal, before anyone
actually pays for Bryan's Normal.

Basically it's just an oddity of returning the Malk after his owner's turn.
If seating were the other way (me, John, Bryan) the Dementia wouldn't change
contest payment patterns, because Bryan wouldn't have had a turn since Normal
became contested.

Josh
